correctness.rationale: For finite-dimensional reduced A0 over Fq, A0 is a product of finite separable fields. The finite-dimensional graded radical is nilpotent, so J0=0 and J^2=0. Semisimplicity of A0⊗F A0^op splits J1 as an A0-bimodule; the resulting complement is closed under multiplication by the grading rule. The Peirce decomposition and associativity argument prove the four-type list. The finite checker confirms the explicit M2(F2) field-grading model, but the all-algebra conclusion rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact reduced-neutral-component hypothesis and resulting radical-splitting theorem were not found in the inspected primary literature or the mathematical database searches. The recent matrix-algebra paper treats the strictly stronger identity x^q=x; older graded-division literature describes simple building blocks rather than this arbitrary-algebra radical criterion. Residual risk remains that a general graded Wedderburn–Mal’tsev theorem implies an equivalent formulation.

value.rationale: Reducedness is a natural structural hypothesis strictly weaker than x^q=x on the neutral component. The theorem identifies when the graded radical is necessarily square-zero, constructs a complement compatible with the grading in characteristic two, and records the additional field-extension components. The result applies to all finite-dimensional associative \(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\)-graded algebras in the stated setting rather than an arbitrary small example.
